original.title: The job demands-resources model of burnout.

core_idea: Every job has demands (workload, emotional pressure) and resources (support, autonomy, feedback). High demands drain energy and lead to burnout and health problems; resources foster engagement and motivation and can buffer the effect of demands. The model is general enough to apply to any occupation.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: What drives burnout or engagement among teachers, nurses, civil servants or other workers?
Which resources buffer the effect of demands in a given job?
Typical data: surveys with validated scales, often longitudinal; interviews for context.
common_mistakes: Picking demands and resources without justifying them for the occupation studied.
Using cross-sectional data to claim causal effects.
Ignoring personal resources and job crafting added later.
